newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Manila market dips, still seen as fragile.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Manila market dips, still seen as fragile.

text.p: Philippine shares drifted downwards on Thursday despite another surge by property issues, and analysts said the market still faced wobbly days ahead.
Bouts of profit-taking at mid-session nullified opening gains and pulled the main index down to close 0.25 percent at 2,906.33.
Analysts and traders said the market, which earlier this week suffered its steepest one-day fall in more than four months, remained susceptible to bad news but the worst might be over.
"I think in terms of bad falls, we probably won't see steep ones in the near term," said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities.
Empire East Land Holdings Inc and parent company Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc, dogged for weeks by rumours of financial problems, advanced for the second straight day.
Analysts attributed the rebound partly to improved sentiment after the firm's assurances that they were not facing bankruptcy.
Empire, the most heavily traded issue, soared 22.11 percent to close at 5.80 pesos while Megaworld rose by 18.75 percent, to 5.70 pesos.

But banks and financial issues skidded 1.69 percent. Analysts said the announcement by unlisted thrift bank Monte de Piedad and Savings Bank of a bank holiday after being hit by two days of heavy withdrawals of deposits helped depress sentiment in the sector.
"It's still a fragile market ... looking for support," analyst Elline Salvatierra of Dharmala Securities Phils Inc said.
A total of 3.9 billion shares worth 2.7 billion pesos changed hands with winners edging losers 83 to 37.
Analysts and traders said they expected the market to trade in a tight band in the next few days.
"It's still an emotional market highly susceptible to bad news," said one analyst.
